=== MY OWN LEAK, AND THE REDACTION OF IT. RESTATED HERE BECAUSE MY NOTES REPLACE THE DISCLOSURE THAT CARRIED IT. ===
My first-pass DISAGREE record on this PR LEAKED A PRIVATE DOMAIN FRAGMENT. Describing a check I had run -- confirming that the private email domain #32's history left behind is absent from this branch -- I quoted the domain fragment verbatim inside the grep command instead of describing it. That is precisely the leak class scripts/lwb_check_env_leak.py exists to catch, committed by the reviewer, inside the very sentence claiming the branch was clean of it. Measured by the author's session, not by me: `python scripts/lwb_check_env_leak.py` -> `FAIL: reviews/41/cloud-reviewer-b.json:10: private-project name leak (needle #3)`.
The PR author's session redacted exactly that one word in commit cd9cf00c5801aa6ff5fa3dcbabe6cc98747ae7b8, in place, changing nothing else -- not the verdict, not either finding, not reviewed_commit, not any identity field -- and appended an addendum disclosing the redaction in full. I have diffed that commit against its parent and confirm the redaction is its only change. The precedent it cites is real and in this repository's history: 5a0cea6 did the same cross-identity against reviews/32/cloud-reviewer-c.json.
I ENDORSE THE REDACTION WITHOUT RESERVATION. A cross-identity privacy redaction of a leaked secret is not evidence tampering, and a reviewer's own record cannot amend itself. Because my notes now replace the author's addendum in this field, the disclosure is restated here in full rather than silently dropped; the original addendum remains in git history at cd9cf00, and the unredacted record remains at fb9022926c6308981ab55a3e33659aec48406bce.
WHAT IS NOT FIXED, AND I WILL NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE: the leaking commit fb90229 is still in this branch's history. Force-push is denied here, so it cannot be removed without a rewrite and none is attempted. If the `--range` variant of the env-leak gate -- the one CI runs over added lines from base.sha to head.sha rather than over the working tree -- fails on this branch, THAT IS MY COMMIT CAUSING IT, not anything the author wrote, and it is the same unrepairable-history situation #32 hit with bbdfccf. I flag it so nobody spends time diagnosing it as a defect in the PR, and so the fact is not quietly absorbed into an apparent pass.
I scanned this record before pushing it: no private fragment appears anywhere in these notes. The lesson generalises and belongs on the record -- a reviewer describing a secret-scanning check must DESCRIBE the needle and never QUOTE it, because the description of the check gets committed to the same repository the check protects.
